resources.string: WrtCtrl is locked, or no router is selected.
WrtCtrl is free and open source. Sponsor development on GitHub
Found a problem or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub
Hide every action that changes something on this router
Flag the router from %1$d%% memory used
Screenshots and screen recordings show a blank screen
The recent apps view shows a blank card instead of the app

Signing in to a router and the lock and PIN screens are always kept out of screenshots and recordings, even with Hide in screenshots off. With the app lock on, the recent apps view always shows a blank card.
Ask for your fingerprint or app PIN before anything that changes a router: Wi-Fi, DHCP, port forwards, services, reboots, upgrades. Once confirmed, the next minute doesn\'t ask again

The app PIN is never stored. It is checked with a key in the phone\'s secure hardware, and after 5 wrong tries you have to wait (30 seconds, doubling up to 15 minutes). Forgot it? The lock screen can remove your routers so you can add them again.
Confirm it\'s you to manage your routers
WrtCtrl is about to change something on your router
Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening WrtCtrl. It\'s separate from your phone\'s PIN
At least %1$d digits, separate from your phone\'s PIN
Only strong biometrics such as your fingerprint, checked by the phone\'s secure hardware. The PIN is still needed after a restart and every 72 hours
Set up a fingerprint on this phone first
As soon as you leave the app
Enter your PIN. It\'s needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Too many tries. Try again in %1$d s

The PIN can\'t be recovered, because it can encrypt your router logins. WrtCtrl will remove every router from this phone and turn the app lock off. Nothing changes on your routers; add them again to continue.
A fingerprint was added or removed. Unlock with your PIN, then turn fingerprint unlock on again.
Couldn\'t unlock with your fingerprint. Use your PIN.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN. If you forget it, the only way back in is to remove your routers and add them again.
WrtCtrl\'s app lock now has its own PIN, separate from your phone\'s. Your router logins can be encrypted with it while the app is locked.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.
Enter your app PIN to turn the lock off.
Too easy to guess. Try a less obvious PIN.
The PINs didn\'t match. Start again.
Couldn\'t save the PIN. Try again.
Unlock with your fingerprint, face or screen lock one last time, then choose an app PIN.
Confirm it\'s you to choose an app PIN
WrtCtrl is about to change something on your router. Enter your app PIN or use your fingerprint.
Router status, WAN, live throughput and the attention list will show here.
Every device on your network, from DHCP leases, host hints and the neighbour table, will show here.
Wi-Fi and the guest network, DHCP leases, port forwards and interfaces will show here.
Services, packages, the system log, reboot and config backups will show here.
Flag the router from %1$d%% of its storage (overlay) used
WrtCtrl signs in to your router\'s ubus API, the same API LuCI uses. A dedicated login that can only do what the app needs is the safest way in: see the README.
The rpcd login, the same as for LuCI. A dedicated login with only the permissions WrtCtrl needs is safer than root.
Type the password again: it\'s only reused for the same address and username.
Enter your router\'s address, like 192.168.1.1 or https://router.lan
Not encrypted (HTTP), how OpenWrt serves LuCI by default. Fine on your home network or a VPN, risky anywhere else. Use https:// if you set up HTTPS on the router.
This login can only look, not change anything, so read-only mode is turned on.
%1$s now presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. Only continue if you replaced or renewed it yourself.
%1$s uses a certificate your phone doesn\'t know, like the self-signed certificate OpenWrt creates for HTTPS.
Check that this SHA-256 fingerprint matches your router\'s (on the router, run: openssl x509 -in /etc/uhttpd.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256):
From now on WrtCtrl only accepts this exact certificate from this router.

%1$s is an http:// address. Then your router password, your session and everything WrtCtrl shows and changes are sent unencrypted, and anyone on the network can read them. That\'s fine on your home network or a VPN, but risky anywhere else. WrtCtrl only uses HTTP for this address.
Switch, add or remove OpenWrt routers
WrtCtrl forgets this router and deletes its saved password from the phone. Nothing changes on the router itself.
This comes from the login\'s rpcd permissions (ACL) on the router. Anything it can\'t do is greyed out in the app.
This login can\'t do anything WrtCtrl needs. Check its permissions in /etc/config/rpcd and /usr/share/rpcd/acl.d (see the README).
Change port forwards and block devices
Can\'t reach %1$s. Check the address and that your phone is on a network that can reach it.
%1$s uses a certificate your phone doesn\'t trust.
Couldn\'t read the certificate %1$s presents, so it can\'t be checked. Try again, or check the address.
%1$s presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. WrtCtrl stopped connecting to protect your sign-in.
This login isn\'t allowed to do this. Check its permissions on the router.
%1$s answered, but not like OpenWrt\'s ubus API. Check the address and port: use the one you open LuCI on, not AdGuard Home\'s.
This router is in read-only mode, so nothing was changed. Turn read-only mode off to make changes.
Cancelled: the change wasn\'t confirmed with your fingerprint or app PIN.
Blocked an unencrypted (HTTP) connection to %1$s. WrtCtrl only uses HTTP for a router address you chose it for.
